PARTICIPATION AT CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS
AS A RESULT OF THE COVID-19 VIRUS, AND RESULTING ORDERS AND DIRECTION FROM THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES, THE GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AND THE ORANGE COUNTY HEALTH CARE AGENCY, AS WELL AS THE CITY OF IRVINE EMERGENCY DECLARATION, THE PUBLIC WILL NOT BE PERMITTED TO PHYSICALLY ATTEND THE IRVINE CITY COUNCIL MEETING TO WHICH THIS AGENDA APPLIES.
YOU MAY SUBMIT COMMENTS ON ANY AGENDA ITEM OR ON ANY ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA, IN WRITING VIA MAIL TO "ATTN: CITY COUNCIL," ONE CIVIC CENTER PLAZA, IRVINE, CA 92606; BY EMAIL TO CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG; OR THROUGH E-COMMENT (SUBMIT COMMENTS BY CLICKING "E-COMMENT" NEXT TO THE ONLINE AGENDA LINK). YOU MAY WATCH THE MEETING LIVE ON ICTV, COX COMMUNICATIONS LOCAL ACCESS CHANNEL 30, AND AT&T U-VERSE CHANNEL 99, AND LIVESTREAMED ONLINE AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV.
PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. IT WOULD BE APPRECIATED IF COMMUNICATIONS OF PUBLIC COMMENTS RELATED TO ITEMS ON THE AGENDA, OR ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA, ARE PROVIDED PRIOR TO THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE MEETING. IF THAT IS NOT POSSIBLE, EVERY EFFORT WILL BE MADE TO ATTEMPT TO REVIEW EMAILS DURING THE COURSE OF THE MEETING. TOWARDS THIS END, THE MAYOR WILL ENDEAVOR TO TAKE A BRIEF PAUSE BEFORE ACTION IS TAKEN ON ANY AGENDA ITEM TO ALLOW THE CITY CLERK TO REVIEW EMAILS, AND SHARE ANY PUBLIC COMMENTS RECEIVED DURING THE MEETING.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk''s Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us . Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City''s system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:

 University Park Center (Culver/Michelson)
 Walnut Village Center (Culver/Walnut)
 Northwood Town Center (Irvine Blvd./Yale)
 City's web page at www.ci.irvine.ca.us

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  March 24, 2020
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:02 p.m. on March 24,
2020, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine,
California; Mayor Shea presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present:  5  Councilmember:  Melissa Fox*
  Councilmember:  Farrah N. Khan
  Councilmember:  Anthony Kuo
  Mayor Pro Tempore:  Mike Carroll
  Mayor:  Christina Shea

  * Via teleconference

Mayor Shea announced for members of the public that the meeting was broadcast live on
ICTV and livestreamed on the City’s website; and noted that in an effort to protect public
health and prevent the spread of the COVID-19 (coronavirus), the City of Irvine had
extended the “e-comment” feature for all agenda items, which would be accepted through
the public discussion portion of each agenda item, read aloud, and included as part of the
official record.
 City Council Minutes  March 24, 2020

  1.  CLOSED SESSION (HELD IN THE CONFERENCE AND TRAINING CENTER)

  City Attorney Melching announced the following Closed Session items:

  1.1  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION:
  Initiation of litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9: One case

  1.2  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION:
  Significant exposure to litigation pursuant to paragraph (2) or (3) of
  subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: One case

  1.3  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS (Pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54957.6) Agency Negotiators: John Russo,
  City Manager; Marianna Marysheva, Assistant City Manager; Michelle
  Grettenberg, Deputy City Manager; Mike Hamel, Director of Public
  Safety/Chief of Police; Jimmee Medina, Director of Human Resources
  & Innovation; Kristin Griffith, Director of Financial Management &
  Strategic Planning; Brian King, Deputy Director of Human Resources;
  Employee Organizations: Associated Supervisory/ Administrative
  Personnel (ASAP); Irvine City Employees Association (ICEA); Irvine
  Professional Employees Association (IPEA); Irvine Police
  Association (IPA); and Irvine Police Management Association (IPMA).

  1.4  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES (Gov. Code Section
  54957): Consultation with Chief of Police and City Attorney

  There were no requests to speak.

  RECESS

  Mayor Shea recessed the City Council meeting to Closed Session at 4:02 p.m.

  RECONVENE TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  Mayor Shea reconvened the City Council meeting at 5:50 p.m. City Attorney Melching, on
  behalf of the City Council, announced that no reportable action was taken in Closed Session.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Vice Mayor Carroll led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Jason Aguilar from Arise Church in Irvine provided the invocation.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  March 24, 2020

  2.  PRESENTATIONS

  Mayor Shea announced that Presentation Item Nos. 2.1 through 2.3 were removed
  from the agenda originally posted on March 12, 2020; however, any proclamations
  associated with these items were included as part of Consent Calendar Item No.
  3.2.

  2.1  Proclaim March 20, 2020, as commencement of "Nowruz - Persian
  New Year"

  2.2  Proclaim April 12-18, 2020,  as  "National  Public  Safety
  Telecommunicators Week"

  2.3  2020 Census Update

  CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  City Manager Russo turned to Assistant City Manager Marysheva, who provided a report
  on various actions taken by City staff to assist in protecting residents and businesses in
  Irvine from the potential effects of the Coronavirus pandemic. Mike Hamel, Chief of Police;
  Laurie Hoffman, Director of Community Services; Mark Steuer, Director of Public Works and
  Transportation; and Pete Carmichael, Director of Community Development, also provided a
  summary of measures taken within their respective departments.

  City Council discussion included: clarifying that while playgrounds were roped off and off
  limits, parks remained open for passive use; and inquired about whether the City could
  remind development partners and others in the construction industry to be cognizant of
  those working from home.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Kuo made the following announcements:

  •  Younger City residents are encouraged to participate in the “Chalk the Walk” effort
  that is underway in several Irvine neighborhoods.

  •  School children participating in online education are also encouraged to find a United
  States flag and start each morning with the Pledge of Allegiance.

  •  As part of “#greatamericantakeout”, Irvine residents are encouraged to support local
  restaurants and our local economy by ordering take-out or delivery.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  March 24, 2020

  Councilmember Fox announced the following:

  •  Noted her participation in several virtual meetings with municipal officials throughout
  California to share ideas and best practices to distribute resources and assist
  vulnerable populations, and as part of that network, was able to develop a supply of
  masks, respirators, gloves, and other personal protective equipment (PPE) for the
  Orange County Fire Authority and area hospitals; and worked with Committee
  Member Zhihai Li and the local Chinese community to coordinate the donation of
  thousands of gloves, masks, and other PPE items. Donated items can be dropped
  off at the Orange County Fire Authority Headquarters, 1 Fire Authority Road, Irvine.

  •  Worked in collaboration with the Orange County Health Department to shut down
  uninspected raw meat sales that were being sold out of the back of the van, and
  encouraged members of the community to refrain from purchasing uninspected raw
  meat, especially during this time.

  Councilmember Fox also inquired about public participation in the City Council meeting
  given that City Hall was closed to the public, to which Molly Perry, City Clerk, noted that
  while a technical issue prevented members of the public from submitting “e-comments” for
  this meeting, comments could be submitted via email at clerk@cityofirvine.org. She also
  noted that any e-comments already received would also be read into the record and included
  in the official record.

  Mayor Shea provided an update on efforts and preventative measures taken related to the
  coronavirus (COVID-19) since the emergency meeting of the City Council held on March
  18, 2020; made the following announcement:

  •  A team of medical researchers at UC Irvine is playing a critical role in finding a way
  to treat COVID-19. Dr. Alpesh Amin and Dr. Lanney Hsieh have been authorized to
  use an anti-viral drug on certain COVID-19 patients hospitalized at UC Irvine Medical
  Center. This is part of a national clinical trial to determine if the drug, remdesvir, is
  effective in treating the illness. The drug had been developed to treat the Ebola virus,
  but it has shown to have to have had some success as coronavirus treatment in some
  acutely ill patients. If the study proves successful, the treatment would go for FDA
  approval. It is also important to know that UC Irvine has the ability to test for COVID-
  19. For those who feel symptomatic, contact your local primary care physician, or call
  UC Irvine’s Patient Access Center at 714-456-7002. Testing is conducted at the UC
  Irvine Medical Center or at the Gottschalk Testing Center on campus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  March 24, 2020

  3.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Moved by Vice Mayor Carroll, seconded by Councilmember Kuo, and
  unanimously carried to approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 3.1 through 3.12,

  5.2  CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST BY MAYOR SHEA AND
  COUNCILMEMBER KHAN TO DISCUSS AN URGENCY ORDINANCE
  ON EVICTION LIMITATIONS DUE TO CORONAVIRUS

  This item was agendized at the request of Mayor Shea and
  Councilmember Khan, who asked for City Council discussion to discuss a
  potential urgency ordinance on eviction limitations due to coronavirus
  (COVID-19).

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, provided a brief summary of recent Federal
  and State provisions and directives, and reiterated that local agencies had
  the ability to make final decisions with respect to eviction limitations based
  on the Governor’s Order. He also noted an errata memo clarifying that the
  proposed resolution would remain in effect until May 31, 2020, unless an
  extension was deemed necessary by further action of the City Council.

  City Council discussion included: noting the need for an urgency ordinance
  to limit evictions due to coronavirus; and discussed options related to
  mortgages.

  During discussion, Councilmember Fox asked for a point of personal
  privilege based on comments made at the dais.

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Vice Mayor
  Carroll, to:

  Deny Councilmember Fox’s request for a point of personal privilege,
  thereby deeming the request out of order.

  The motion carried as follows:

  AYES:  4 COUNCILMEMBERS:  Carroll, Khan, Kuo and Shea

  NOES:  1 COUNCILMEMBERS:  Fox

  ABSENT: 0 COUNCILMEMBERS:  None

  property; inquired about assistance for University of California, Irvine
  students; questioned the legal enforceability of the proposed resolution;
  discussed cooperation versus regulation; reiterated that the proposed

  5.3  CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST BY MAYOR SHEA AND
  COUNCILMEMBER KHAN TO DISCUSS A RESOLUTION PROPOSING
  PREVENTIVE MEASURES

  This item was agendized at the request of Mayor Shea and
  Councilmember Khan, who asked for City Council support for a resolution
  listing additional local preventive measures reflected in their memo to
  ensure the safety of the community, which would be in addition to actions
  by the City Council at its emergency meeting on March12, 2020, and the
  declaration of emergency issued on March 18, 2020.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, provided a brief summary of the intention of
  the resolution submitted by Mayor Shea and Councilmember Khan.

  City Council discussion included: expressing appreciation to those deemed
  as essential workers; inquired about whether curbside pickup was
  permitted in Irvine; noted the importance of requiring masks and gloves for
  essential retail workers to protect residents, business owners, and
  employees; noted concerns raised by retail workers; suggested that the
  resolution be amended to encourage employers to offer mental health
  resources available to their employees through the County; and reiterated
  that many large retailers, including but not limited to Ralphs, Albertsons,
  Gelsons, Target, and Whole Foods, were offering special shopping hours
  for seniors and other vulnerable populations.

  Molly Perry, City Clerk, read into the record an “e-comment” submitted by
  Lori DiCarlo, Irvine resident, who spoke in support of the resolution; and
  suggested measures to protect seniors and other vulnerable populations
  from hoarding, and also suggested a proclamation of support for those who
  remain on the job to serve the community.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  14
 City Council Minutes  March 24, 2020

  City Clerk Perry noted that due to technological issues, Councilmember
  Fox was absent for a portion of discussion related to this item; however,
  Councilmember Fox was contacted via telephone, who offered her support
  of the item.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Khan, seconded by Mayor Shea,
  and unanimously carried to:

  Adopt RESOLUTION NO. 20-30 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, PROPOSING
  PREVENTATIVE MEASURES TO PREVENT AND COMBAT THE
  SPREAD OF COVID-19 as amended to:

  1) Include the most up-to-date statistics related to number of
  confirmed cases and deaths related to COVID-19;
  2) Strongly encourage all local businesses to provide information
  to their employees on mental health resources that are
  available throughout the County, to help cope with the
  stresses caused by the COVID-19 emergency.
